A1.justification: Both readable ten-page PDFs describe the same GMValuator study, with corresponding equations, Algorithm 1, Figures 1–3, and Table 1. All pages were inspected; both documents end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original CIFAR-10 distribution and data-value analyses (Figure 2 and Table 1), alongside CelebA image-matching examples (Figure 3).

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original CIFAR-10 analyses and CelebA image-matching results in Figure 2, Table 1, and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same product-quantization similarity matching, top-k selection, contribution scoring, and aggregation procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain the CIFAR-10 training-versus-nontraining comparisons and CelebA face-matching examples. The MNIST description is also unchanged; no dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing data-valuation methods; methods such as Shapley valuation remain discussion-only. The same BigGAN, classifier-free guidance diffusion, and StyleGAN2 evaluations are retained.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 retain the same CIFAR-10 partition design, generator choices, VGG-16 embeddings with t-SNE, and CelebA matching procedure. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The distribution visualization in Figure 2 and high-value versus low-value image case study in Figure 3 are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, or robustness test is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 and Table 1 retain the same hypothesis-testing procedure and significance-threshold reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains training/nontraining means of 1.632352/0.319654 for BigGAN and 0.369565/0.030434 for classifier-free guidance diffusion, with identical p-values and t-statistics. Figures 2–3 and their reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The IID assumption, Wasserstein formulation, and scoring and aggregation definitions in Equations 1–6 are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion preserve the same novelty, model-agnostic applicability, training-free valuation, and experimental-effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of RA1–RA3 and Section 6's proposed privacy, content-pricing, and intellectual-property applications are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information are unchanged. The new acknowledgment of an NVIDIA Hardware Award does not specify experimental hardware, hyperparameters, or code/data access.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 30 cited works, and the positioning relative to prior data-valuation research remain unchanged. Reference relocation does not introduce additional literature.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 8, Acknowledgments, between the conclusion and references, crediting NSERC, Public Safety Canada, and NVIDIA. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and narrative structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments block shifts the reference layout on pages 9–10, moving entries 14–15 onto page 10. Other differences are minor text reflow; Figures 1–3, Table 1, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: The added acknowledgments provide funding attribution, while the method, evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The limited layout changes neither materially improve nor harm readability, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
